topic: 5 things you need to know: the Justice Department's new Super Intelligence Task Force
post:
The US Justice Department now has a task force with "Super Intelligence" in its name. 🏛️
Here are 5 things you need to know.

1️⃣ What it is
The DOJ announced the Super Intelligence Task Force (DOJ-SITF) to make sure US AI technology isn't compromised or misused by foreign actors or fraudsters.

2️⃣ It coordinates enforcement
The task force will coordinate criminal investigations and civil enforcement involving AI across the department.

3️⃣ It absorbs an earlier unit
It takes over the DOJ's AI Litigation Task Force, which was set up earlier this year to challenge state AI laws in federal court. ⚖️

4️⃣ It links to the White House
The DOJ says it will act as the department's liaison to the White House's broader "Super Intelligence" effort.

5️⃣ Key details are still missing
The DOJ hasn't said how many staff it will have, what it costs, or which AI crimes it will tackle first. 🔍

Why it matters:
AI is now a law enforcement priority, not just a tech topic. And with the earlier unit folded in, it's also part of the fight over who gets to regulate AI: states or Washington.

Practical takeaway:
If your company uses AI, document what tools you use and how. Clear records are your best friend when rules are still forming. 📝

Should AI rules be set by states or nationally? 👇
